newsitem.title: FRANCE: Higher dollar not a blessing for all French firms.
newsitem.headline: Higher dollar not a blessing for all French firms.

text.p: The dollar's rapid rise in the first half of the year has brought a smile on the face of many a French finance director. But some are rather pleased the greenback's rise seems to end.
The dollar started the year at 5.20 francs and climbed to a high of 6.35 on August 8 and was 5.87 francs on June 30 when most first half accounts were closed.
"On average, some 30 percent of the profits of French companies is dollar-related," said Jean-Pascal Rolandez at Paribas.
A recent study by Paribas showed that of the 120 companies in the SBF-120 index, weighted for market value, a rise in the dollar would work through for 30 percent in total profitability.
On this basis, the dollar's 20 percent rise since the start of the year has added six percent to the total profitability of the SBF-120.

Over the same time the SBF-120 share index gained 59 percent to 2,081.48 on August 7 from 1,303.55 on January 2, reflecting a general rise in stock markets, the political climate in France as well as improved profit forecasts.

The effect of the dollar is not the same for all companies. Oil groups Total SA and Elf Aquitaine gain most from the rise. Paribas said the companies' profits were respectively 70 and 60 percent exposed to the dollar.

At Total, a rise of 0.50 centimes in the dollar adds 900 million francs to the annual operating profit. Therefor the gain in the first half of 1997 should add 1.8 billion to the operating profit if the dollar remains at current levels.
At Elf, a rise of 50 centimes would add 1.5 billion francs to the annual operating income, or at least three billion for the dollar's rise so far.
Bouygues Offshore, Technip are also among the gainers.
But tobacco group Seita, property companies, building groups and media groups are hardly affected by the dollar while other companies are actually hurt by the dollar.
Primagaz, a distributor of natural gas, is likely to be hurt because of the increase in raw material costs, analysts said.

Natexis said in a recent study that other companies set to be hurt by a higher dollar are tyre group Michelin, aircraft equipment maker Zodiac, aluminium group Pechiney, plastic group Plastic Omnium and appliance makers SEB and Moulinex.
The precise impact of the dollar's rise will to a large extent depend on the exchange risk cover companies have taken.

At chemicals and drugs group Rhone-Poulenc, which normally would benefit from a dollar rise, managing director Igor Landau said the influence in the first half was limited due to the company's currency positions taken at the start of the year.
Landau expects a bigger impact on earnings from the dollar rise in the second half.

At cognac group Remy-Cointreau the company's currency position went wrong. It made a 158 million franc loss on exchange rate options in the first half and said it would benefit only partly from a dollar rise in the second half.
